title: InspectService refactor: extract inspect/* modules (tests first)
description:
## Problem
`/Users/btraut/Development/browser-bridge/packages/core/src/inspect.ts` is ~2171 lines and currently owns too many responsibilities:
- tab resolution + target hint heuristics
- error mapping and state transitions
- DOM snapshots (AX + HTML fallback), selector scoping, filters, truncation
- snapshot ref assignment + DOM mutation (`data-bv-ref`)
- dom diff/history bookkeeping
- console event shaping
- network HAR shaping + artifact IO
- JS evaluation
- content extraction (Readability + Turndown)
- page state capture
- performance metrics
- screenshot capture + artifact IO

This has become the Core "god object" and is the main maintainability hotspot.

## Recommendation / Approach
Do this as a low-churn refactor with behavior locks:

1. Expand test coverage for the public API surface first.
   - Add/extend tests for: `networkHar()`, `screenshot()`, `extractContent()`, `pageState()`, `performanceMetrics()`.
   - Add tests for AX -> HTML fallback behavior and selector-not-found edge cases.

2. Extract cohesive modules (or small helper classes) while keeping a single orchestration facade.
   - Keep `InspectService` as the facade that owns: session validation, tab resolution, error wrapping, drive mutex usage for `quiesce`, and session state transitions.
   - Move implementation detail clusters out of the facade into separate modules under `packages/core/src/inspect/` (suggested):
     - `har.ts` (HAR building)
     - `ax-snapshot.ts` (filters/truncation/node helpers)
     - `snapshot-refs.ts` (ref assignment + DOM attribute application)
     - `console.ts` (console event -> `ConsoleEntry` shaping)
     - `html-snapshot.ts` (HTML capture + selector handling)

3. Keep the external API stable.
   - No changes to tool names, routes, schemas, or return envelopes.

## Refactoring Steps
1. Add the missing tests (so refactors are gated).
2. Extract `buildHar` into `packages/core/src/inspect/har.ts` with unit tests for core cases.
3. Extract AX snapshot helpers (filters + truncation + node shaping) into `packages/core/src/inspect/ax-snapshot.ts` with unit tests.
4. Extract snapshot ref logic (`assignRefsToAxSnapshot`, `applySnapshotRefs`, selector node resolve helpers) into `packages/core/src/inspect/snapshot-refs.ts`.
5. Extract console shaping helpers into `packages/core/src/inspect/console.ts`.
6. Reduce `/packages/core/src/inspect.ts` to mostly orchestration + composition.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `/Users/btraut/Development/browser-bridge/packages/core/src/inspect.ts` is reduced to a facade/orchestrator (target: <= ~500-700 lines).
- Implementation detail clusters are moved into `packages/core/src/inspect/*` modules.
- No single module becomes a new 1k+ line hotspot.
- Tests cover the previously untested public methods (network HAR, screenshot, extract content, page state, performance metrics).
- All existing tests pass.
design: Low-churn maintainability refactor: lock behavior with tests first, then extract cohesive helper modules; keep InspectService as a facade to avoid dependency explosion and duplicated tab/session/error handling.
close_reason: All child tasks completed: tests expanded, inspect/* modules extracted, and inspect.ts reduced to facade; full test suite passing.

title: Implement WebSocket heartbeat/ping-pong
description:
## Problem
There's no periodic ping/pong to detect stale WebSocket connections. WebSocket close events aren't always delivered promptly, especially on network issues.

## Solution
Implement heartbeat mechanism:
1. Core sends ping every 15 seconds
2. Extension responds with pong
3. If no pong received within 5 seconds, consider connection stale
4. Trigger reconnection on stale detection

## Files to Modify
- `packages/core/src/extension-bridge.ts` - Add ping sender, pong handler
- `packages/extension/src/background.ts` - Add ping handler, pong sender
- `packages/core/src/drive-protocol.ts` - Add ping/pong message types

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Heartbeat sent every 15 seconds
- [ ] Stale connection detected within 20 seconds
- [ ] Automatic reconnection on stale detection
- [ ] No impact on normal operation latency
close_reason: Closed

title: Add inspect.extract_content for Readability + Markdown
description:
Add intelligent content extraction using Mozilla's Readability algorithm and Turndown markdown conversion. This dramatically improves LLM comprehension of web pages.

## Problem
- Hamburg's `inspect.dom_snapshot` returns raw HTML or accessibility tree
- Raw HTML is noisy (nav, ads, scripts, boilerplate)
- LLMs work much better with clean, structured markdown

## Solution
Add new tool `inspect.extract_content`:

```typescript
{
  name: "inspect.extract_content",
  input: {
    format: "markdown" | "text" | "article_json",
    include_metadata?: boolean
  },
  output: {
    content: string,
    title?: string,
    byline?: string,
    excerpt?: string,
    siteName?: string
  }
}
```

## Implementation

### Dependencies
```bash
npm install @mozilla/readability turndown jsdom
```

### Processing Pipeline
1. Get page HTML via existing inspect mechanism
2. Parse with JSDOM
3. Extract article content with Readability
4. Convert to markdown with Turndown
5. Return clean content + metadata

### Example (from browser-mcp)
```typescript
import { Readability } from "@mozilla/readability";
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
import TurndownService from "turndown";

const dom = new JSDOM(html, { url });
const reader = new Readability(dom.window.document);
const article = reader.parse();
const turndown = new TurndownService();
const markdown = turndown.turndown(article.content);
```

## Where to Implement
- Add new handler in `packages/core/src/inspect.ts`
- Add route in `packages/core/src/routes/inspect.ts`
- Add schema in `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts`
- Wire up in MCP adapter

## Reference
- browser-mcp implementation: /Users/btraut/Downloads/browser-mcp-main/server/tools.ts
- Comparison report: .context/browser-mcp-comparison.md
notes: Decision: keep extract_content in-scope; high-value LLM comprehension win.
close_reason: Closed

title: browser-mcp Feature Parity
description:
Adopt valuable features from external browser-mcp projects that we currently lack. Based on comprehensive comparison of two different projects:

## Projects Compared

### 1. djyde/browser-mcp (content extraction focus)
- ~500 LOC, 5 tools
- Strengths: Content extraction (Readability + Turndown markdown), browser history search
- Analysis: `.context/browser-mcp-comparison.md`

### 2. browsermcp/mcp (interaction focus)  
- ~640 LOC, 13 tools
- Strengths: ARIA snapshot after every action, hover/drag/select/keypress tools
- Analysis: `.context/browsermcp-comparison.md`

## Key Insights

### From djyde/browser-mcp:
1. **Content Extraction** - Readability + Turndown for LLM-friendly markdown output
2. **Service Worker Keep-Alive** - Prevents Chrome from suspending the extension
3. **Browser History Search** - Optional permission for research tasks

### From browsermcp/mcp:
1. **ARIA Snapshot After Actions** - Every interaction returns updated page state automatically
2. **Missing Interaction Tools** - hover, drag, select, keypress, history navigation
3. **Snapshot Mode Toggle** - Optional flag to include/exclude page state in responses

## Architecture Note
- djyde/browser-mcp uses WXT framework for multi-browser builds (Chrome, Edge, Firefox)
- browsermcp/mcp uses simple tool factory pattern for consistency

## Priority
High-value items: Content extraction, service worker keep-alive, hover/drag/select tools
Medium-value: ARIA snapshot pattern, keypress, history nav
Low-value: History search, bookmarks, CSS injection tool
notes:

title: Add include_snapshot option to drive tools
description:
Add optional parameter to drive tools to automatically return DOM snapshot after action.

## Source
browsermcp/mcp's key innovation: every interaction tool returns ARIA snapshot automatically.

## Pattern
```typescript
// Current: action returns minimal response
drive.click({ locator }) -> { ok: true }

// With option: action returns page state
drive.click({ locator, include_snapshot: true }) -> { 
  ok: true, 
  snapshot: { ... } 
}
```

## Why This Matters
AI agents almost always need to see the result of their action. Current pattern requires:
1. `drive.click(...)` 
2. `inspect.dom_snapshot(...)`

With this option:
1. `drive.click({ ..., include_snapshot: true })`

**Saves a round-trip on every interaction.**

## Implementation Options

### Option A: Parameter on each tool
Add `include_snapshot?: boolean` to all drive tool schemas.

### Option B: Session-level setting
```typescript
session.configure({ auto_snapshot: true })
```
Then all drive actions return snapshot.

### Option C: Compound tools
Create `drive.click_and_observe`, `drive.type_and_observe` variants.

## Recommendation
Start with Option A (parameter) for flexibility. Can add Option B later.

## Scope
Affects: `drive.click`, `drive.type`, `drive.scroll`, `drive.navigate`, `drive.hover`, `drive.drag`, `drive.select`, `drive.key`

title: Add inspect.extract_content for LLM-friendly markdown
description:
Add intelligent content extraction using Mozilla's Readability algorithm and Turndown markdown conversion.

## Source
djyde/browser-mcp's key differentiator is content extraction:
```typescript
const dom = new JSDOM(html, { url });
const reader = new Readability(dom.window.document);
const article = reader.parse();
const markdown = turndownService.turndown(article.content);
```

## Current Gap
`inspect.dom_snapshot` returns raw HTML or accessibility tree. LLMs struggle with:
- Navigation elements
- Ads and boilerplate
- Complex HTML structure
- Verbose markup

## Schema
```typescript
const ExtractContentSchema = z.object({
  format: z.enum(['markdown', 'text', 'article_json']).default('markdown'),
  include_metadata: z.boolean().default(true),
  session_id: z.string().uuid().optional(),
});

{
  content: string,      // Clean markdown/text
  title?: string,       // Article title
  byline?: string,      // Author
  excerpt?: string,     // Summary
  site_name?: string,   // Publisher
  length?: number,      // Word count
}
```

## Implementation

### Option A: Server-side (Recommended)
1. Get HTML via `inspect.dom_snapshot`
2. Process with `@mozilla/readability` and `turndown` in Core
3. Return clean markdown

### Option B: Extension-side
1. Inject Readability into page
2. Extract in content script
3. Convert in background

Option A is simpler and keeps extension lightweight.

## Dependencies
```json
{
  "@mozilla/readability": "^0.5.0",
  "turndown": "^7.1.2",
  "jsdom": "^24.0.0"
}
```

## Why High Priority
This would **dramatically improve** page comprehension tasks. LLMs work far better with clean markdown than raw HTML or accessibility trees.

## Use Cases
- Summarizing articles
- Extracting key information
- Research and fact-finding
- Content analysis

title: Add drive.fill_form for batch form filling
description:
Add a tool that fills multiple form fields in a single call with smart type detection and detailed error reporting.

## Why
Single tool call vs multiple drive.type calls. Reduces latency, tokens, and handles complex forms (checkboxes, selects, radios) elegantly.

## YetiBrowser Reference
File: /Users/btraut/Downloads/yetibrowser-mcp-main/extensions/shared/src/background/index.ts
- Function: fillFormFields (around line 800+)
- Handles: text, select, checkbox, radio, contentEditable
- Auto-detects field type
- Boolean coercion for checkboxes ('true', '1', 'yes', 'on' → true)

## Implementation

### 1. Schema (packages/shared/src/schemas.ts)
```typescript
const FormFieldSchema = z.object({
  selector: z.string(), // CSS selector or locator
  value: z.union([z.string(), z.boolean()]),
  type: z.enum(['auto', 'text', 'select', 'checkbox', 'radio', 'contentEditable']).optional().default('auto'),
  submit: z.boolean().optional().default(false) // submit form after this field
});

const FillFormInputSchema = z.object({
  fields: z.array(FormFieldSchema),
  tab_id: z.number().optional()
});

const FillFormResultSchema = z.object({
  filled: z.number(),
  attempted: z.number(),
  errors: z.array(z.string())
});
```

### 2. Content Script (packages/extension/src/content.ts)
Add fillFormFields function:
- detectFieldType(element): Determine input type from tagName, type attribute
- coerceBoolean(value): Handle string→boolean conversion
- setInputValue(el, value): Set value and dispatch input/change events
- selectOption(el, value): Handle <select> by value or text
- setCheckbox(el, checked): Handle checkbox/radio

### 3. Drive Protocol (packages/core/src/drive-protocol.ts)
- Add 'fill_form' action type

### 4. Extension Background (packages/extension/src/background.ts)
- Handle fill_form action, call content script

### 5. Route (packages/core/src/routes/drive.ts)
- Add /drive/fill_form endpoint

### 6. MCP + CLI
- Add drive.fill_form tool
- Add fill-form CLI subcommand

## Example Usage
```json
{
  "fields": [
    { "selector": "#email", "value": "test@example.com" },
    { "selector": "#country", "value": "USA", "type": "select" },
    { "selector": "#terms", "value": true, "type": "checkbox" },
    { "selector": "#bio", "value": "Hello world", "submit": true }
  ]
}
```

Returns: { filled: 4, attempted: 4, errors: [] }

title: [Decision] WebSocket authentication approach
description:
## Problem
The WebSocket connection between extension and core has no authentication. Any local process that knows the port can connect.

Current security relies solely on:
- Localhost binding (127.0.0.1)
- Random port or configurable port

## Risk Assessment
- **Severity**: Medium (local-only attack surface)
- **Likelihood**: Low (requires malicious local process)
- **Impact**: High (full browser control if exploited)

## Solution Options
1. **Shared secret in storage**
   - Core generates random token on startup
   - Extension reads from known file/env
   - Token required in WebSocket handshake
   
2. **Extension ID verification**
   - Core verifies connecting client is the expected extension
   - Requires custom handshake protocol

## Design Decision Needed
This may be acceptable for v1 local-only use. Document the security model and defer implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Security model documented
- [ ] If implementing: token-based auth on WebSocket
- [ ] If deferring: explicit docs noting this limitation

title: [Decision] Per-session vs global drive mutex
description:
## Problem
Global singleton mutex (`drive.ts:23`):
```typescript
export const driveMutex = new DriveMutex();
```

All drive operations across all sessions serialize through one mutex. This means:
- Session A's long operation blocks Session B
- No parallelism even for independent sessions

## Solution
Move mutex to per-session level:
1. Store mutex in `SessionRecord`
2. Each session has independent drive serialization
3. Global mutex only for cross-session operations (if any)

## Trade-offs
- **Pro**: Better parallelism for multi-session use
- **Con**: More complexity in session lifecycle
- **Con**: May cause issues if sessions share Chrome state

## Design Decision Needed
Evaluate if multi-session parallelism is needed. Document decision.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Design decision documented
- [ ] If implementing: per-session mutex
- [ ] If deferring: document limitation
close_reason: Decision: keep a single global drive mutex. Sessions are not tab-bound/isolated; many extension actions default to active tab when tab_id is omitted, so per-session parallelism would be unsafe. Revisit if we make sessions tab-affine or switch to per-tab mutex with required tab_id.

title: Add --max-nodes to inspect dom-snapshot
description: Some clients/tools attempt to call: browser-bridge inspect dom-snapshot ... --max-nodes <n>. Today this fails with 'unknown option --max-nodes'. Add first-class support to bound snapshot size (primarily AX trees) for LLM/agent consumption.
design:
Proposed behavior
- Add CLI flag: browser-bridge inspect dom-snapshot --max-nodes <n>
- Wire through to Core inspect.domSnapshot as optional max_nodes.
- AX format only: after existing filters (interactive/compact) apply truncation so returned AX snapshot contains <= n nodes.
- If truncation occurs, add a warning (and optionally a boolean like truncated=true if we want a structured signal).
- HTML format: ignore max_nodes and add warning: max_nodes is only supported for AX snapshots.

Truncation algorithm (AX)
- Work with AX snapshot shapes returned by Accessibility.getFullAXTree / getPartialAXTree (array or { nodes: [...] }).
- Build nodeById (nodeId -> node), and compute parent counts from childIds.
- Roots are nodes with parentCount==0; if none, fall back to first node as root.
- BFS from roots, keeping nodes until limit is reached. Keep set of kept nodeIds.
- Output snapshot with nodes filtered to kept set.
- For each kept node, prune childIds to kept set (similar to existing filter logic).

- /Users/btraut/Development/browser-bridge/packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:
  - Add max_nodes?: number to InspectDomSnapshotInputSchema.
